clauses.reason: The order's lead command is that the clause 'shall become effective as a part of any code of fair competition approved under said Title'. It is a standing prescription whose only operation is inside an approved code, which under section 3 had legal effect as the standards of fair competition (3(b)), was enforceable by injunction (3(c)) and by misdemeanor prosecution (3(f)). Section 2 of S.J. Res. 113, approved June 14, 1935, provides: "All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed". After that date no code could be approved or enforced under Title I, so the lead command had no further operation on June 14, 1935. No held record shows it ended earlier, and June 16, 1935 is not an end because section 1 of the resolution replaced that expiry with April 1, 1936.

Section 1 of the clause authorizes the Code Authority to support the administration of the code through the steps in paragraphs (a) to (c), 'subject to the approval of the Administrator'. It is text of the clause that the lead command makes effective only as a part of an approved code ('the Code Authority is authorized, subject to the approval of the Administrator'), so it operated only through the code's section 3 effect. Section 2 of S.J. Res. 113, approved June 14, 1935, provides: "All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed". The provision therefore ceased to have operative effect on June 14, 1935. No held record shows it ended earlier, and June 16, 1935 is not an end because section 1 of the resolution replaced that expiry with April 1, 1936.

Paragraph (a) authorizes the Code Authority to incur reasonable obligations for administration and to meet them from funds raised under the clause. It is text of the clause that the lead command makes effective only as a part of an approved code ('To incur such reasonable obligations as are necessary and proper'), so it operated only through the code's section 3 effect. Section 2 of S.J. Res. 113, approved June 14, 1935, provides: "All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed". The provision therefore ceased to have operative effect on June 14, 1935. No held record shows it ended earlier, and June 16, 1935 is not an end because section 1 of the resolution replaced that expiry with April 1, 1936.

Paragraph (b) lets the Code Authority submit an itemized budget and an equitable basis of contribution to the Administrator for approval. It is text of the clause that the lead command makes effective only as a part of an approved code ('To submit to the Administrator for his approval'), so it operated only through the code's section 3 effect. Section 2 of S.J. Res. 113, approved June 14, 1935, provides: "All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed". The provision therefore ceased to have operative effect on June 14, 1935. No held record shows it ended earlier, and June 16, 1935 is not an end because section 1 of the resolution replaced that expiry with April 1, 1936.

Paragraph (c) lets the Code Authority, after approval of the budget and basis, determine and secure equitable contributions from industry members and sue for them in its own name. It is text of the clause that the lead command makes effective only as a part of an approved code ('to determine and secure equitable contribution as above set forth by all such members of the Industry'), so it operated only through the code's section 3 effect. Section 2 of S.J. Res. 113, approved June 14, 1935, provides: "All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed". The provision therefore ceased to have operative effect on June 14, 1935. No held record shows it ended earlier, and June 16, 1935 is not an end because section 1 of the resolution replaced that expiry with April 1, 1936.

Section 2 limits participation in selecting the Code Authority, receipt of its voluntary activities and use of the National Recovery Administration emblem to members that comply with the code and contribute. It is text of the clause that the lead command makes effective only as a part of an approved code ('Only members of the Industry complying with the Code and contributing to the expenses of its administration'), so it operated only through the code's section 3 effect. Section 2 of S.J. Res. 113, approved June 14, 1935, provides: "All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed". The provision therefore ceased to have operative effect on June 14, 1935. No held record shows it ended earlier, and June 16, 1935 is not an end because section 1 of the resolution replaced that expiry with April 1, 1936.

research_rationale:
EO 6678 was read in full in the registered APP transcription (common-crawl capture 2025-12-14T13:52:27Z). Identity: the census register row, the WPA 1944 numbered list (1934 Apr 14, p. 574, 'Provisions to meet the expenses incurred in the administration of any code of fair competition by the various code authorities, prescribed') and the APP page record with the same sha256 agree on number, date and subject; the page heading names the order's number, its date matches, and the page record's text_sha256 equals the held file's. The order prescribes, under Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act and 'in order to effectuate the purposes of said Title', a clause on collecting the expenses of code administration. It orders that the clause or an appropriate modification 'shall become effective as a part of any code of fair competition approved under said Title', on application under the code's amendment provisions or by representative trade associations, if the Administrator finds the clause necessary to effectuate the policy of Title I. Section 1 of the clause authorizes the Code Authority, subject to the Administrator's approval, to incur obligations, to submit a budget and a basis of contribution, and to secure contributions, including by suit in its own name; section 2 limits participation in selecting the Code Authority and use of the NRA emblem to members that comply with the code and contribute. It is a general rule for all approved codes rather than the approval of one named code, so the shared analysis does not decide it directly; it is treated here as a code-dependent standing prescription because every command in it takes effect only as part of an approved code. Under the shared reviewed analysis (SHARED_ANALYSIS.md, ADJUDICATION.json) a code-dependent command that did not end earlier ended on June 14, 1935, when section 2 of S.J. Res. 113 repealed the power to approve or prescribe codes and the provisions enforcing them; Schechter (May 27, 1935) is recorded only as a validity characterization. Original not yet held; the working text is a labeled transcription under the 2026-10-21 owner ruling.
